text:
maria: quick heads-up, onboarding raven-4b-qat into prod evals. function-calling JSON compliance is failing ~35% on strict schema tests

samir: ugh. failing how? sample outputs?

maria: pasted one failing output below:
```
{"action": "create_ticket", "params": {title: \"Crash on upload\", description: \"stack trace...\"
}
```
(missing quotes around title key + missing closing brace)

amit: this smells like tokenization boundary issues after QAT. quantized model sometimes emits unescaped quotes or drops trailing tokens, so we get truncated JSON or unquoted keys.

katie: can you grep for common patterns? trailing commas, unquoted keys, stray text after JSON? we can try a repair layer before strict schema failure.
maria: yep ran quick heuristics over 500 samples:
- raw failure rate: 35%
- simple rescue (extract first {...} substring or fix trailing commas): reduces to 10%
- full jsonrepair heuristics (add quotes, close braces, remove trailing junk): down to 4% but introduces occasional semantic drift

eval-bot: automated eval summary: dataset=funcall-evals-2k, model=raven-4b-qat, strict_schema_pass=65%, rescue_pass=96%, downstream-tool-success(after repair)=93%, fidelity_approx_drop=0.8%

samir: 0.8% fidelity drop is acceptable if tool success jumps to 93%. can we scope repair so it only runs when strict_schema fails?

amit: yes. proposal: retry pipeline -> 1) strict parse, 2) attempt lightweight repair (substring extraction + balance braces), 3) if still failing, run jsonrepair heuristics (quote keys, remove trailing commas), 4) last resort: return raw_text to caller with error flag so product can decide

katie: also add telemetry tags for which heuristic fixed it (substring|balance|quote|strip). need to track false positives where repair changes semantics.
maria: one more wrinkle: function-calling requires not just valid JSON but matching schema. repaired JSON often passes JSON.parse but violates schema (missing required params). we should implement a schema-aware repair loop: try to infer missing fields with low-confidence placeholders or call tool with partial params + ask for confirmation.
samir: can we instead fallback to a different model variant for funcalls? e.g., raven-4b-fp16 (non-QAT) as hot fallback for strict routes? slower but more stable.
amit: yes we already have routable variants. routing policy idea: prefer fast qat, but on repeated schema failure escalate to fp16 variant for that user/session for N requests.
katie: action items:
- PR: add schema_rescue boolean and telemetry tags to function-calling runtime (owner: maria)
- experiment: run full 2k eval set with rescue on vs off, compare downstream tool success and fidelity (owner: eval-bot, deadline EOD Tue)
- routing change: implement per-session fallback to non-quant variant after 3 consecutive schema failures (owner: samir)

maria: creating PR now: https://git.internal/redwood/runtimes/pulls/3421 (WIP)

eval-bot: queued job 1769123456-qual-run. will post final numbers here when done. ETA ~3h.

samir: thanks. if numbers look good let's ship rescue as opt-in for staging, then enable on a small % in prod. :thumbsup:

katie: also add a short README with example repaired patterns so reviewers can eyeball changes.
maria: yep adding tests for each pattern + integration test where repaired output is fed to the real tool. will note known failure modes in PR.

amit: one more note for quant team: track tokenization diffs between fp16 and qat for the anchor prompts used in funcall evals. I can produce a token-diff report after the run.
maria: perfect. will follow up after eval-bot finishes.
eval-bot: finished job 1769123456-qual-run. results: strict_schema_pass=66%, rescue_pass=95.8%, downstream_tool_success=92.9%, fidelity_drop=0.77%. full report uploaded to: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/evals/1769123456-report.pdf
samir: those look good. moving to opt-in staging if no objections.
katie: go for it. :rocket:
